Can you approve a limited exception to the copying and disclosure restrictions for selection review? Four festival programmers and one outside accessibility reviewer would have individual, confidential access to the unfinished screener. Two of those five need one offline copy each on encrypted equipment. The other three can stream only. We can identify all five to you privately before granting access and require each to agree in writing to confidentiality and no onward sharing.

We propose closing access and deleting the two offline copies when review ends. The platform retains a backup for 30 days after deletion. We’d need your approval for that retention period. The selection board would hear a short synopsis in a closed session. If you prefer to supply the wording, we can use yours.

If the film is selected, can our publicity staff draft the catalog entry confidentially before the announcement? We can send you the draft for factual corrections and hold publication until the agreed selection announcement. This would let the catalog appear with the announcement even if the film’s public release comes later.

For the selection review, we can approve access to the unfinished screener for the five identified reviewers under the conditions you've outlined: individual, confidential access, written confidentiality agreements, and either streaming or encrypted offline copies with a deletion record. We require confirmation of the reviewers' identities before access is granted.

Regarding the offline copies, we agree to deletion upon review completion and accept a 30-day backup retention period after deletion, pending our approval. We approve the 30-day retention.

For the synopsis to be shared with the selection board, we can provide a short, approved summary to be read out in the closed session.

If the film is selected, we can allow your publicity staff to draft the catalog entry confidentially before the announcement, provided you send us the draft for factual corrections. However, we must approve the final wording. To maintain confidentiality of the ending and cast cameo as per our private agreement with the financier, we'll need to review the draft closely.

We propose that the embargo on publicity materials is lifted upon the agreed selection announcement. We require the ability to withdraw a cut suddenly, so we need a commitment that all draft materials will be deleted upon our request, with a record of deletion provided to us.

To facilitate this, we need a clear understanding that you will not share or publish any excerpts or materials without our prior approval, especially concerning the ending and cast cameo. We'll clear draft copy within two business days.

Let's discuss the specifics of the draft catalog entry and the publicity excerpts to ensure we're aligned on what's permissible under the embargo.

We accept the review terms. We’ll send you the names of the four programmers and the outside accessibility reviewer, identifying the two who need offline access. Access will begin once you confirm the names and each reviewer has signed a confidentiality agreement. Two reviewers may each keep one copy on encrypted equipment. The other three will stream only. Please send the approved synopsis for a programmer to read aloud to the selection board in closed session.

If the film is selected, our publicity staff will use your synopsis and approved credits to draft a text-only catalog entry. We’ll omit the ending and cast cameo and send you the complete entry for factual corrections and written approval of the final wording. We accept your two-business-day review window. If approval is still pending at announcement time, we’ll hold the entry. We’re requesting no clips, stills or quotations. Any future use of those materials would require separate written approval.

On withdrawal, we’ll immediately revoke screener access, halt pending publication and instruct both offline reviewers to delete their copies. We’ll delete the active platform copy and all festival-held drafts, collect the reviewers’ deletion records and send you a record identifying what was deleted, when, and the expiry date of the approved 30-day platform backup. At normal review completion, we’ll follow the same screener deletion process.

Please confirm that the backup exception also applies on withdrawal, and that we may publish the exact approved catalog text once the agreed selection announcement occurs. If you withdraw the cut after publication, we can remove the entry from festival-controlled channels. Copies already obtained by the public are outside our control.

We confirm the names and confidentiality agreements are required before granting access to the screener. We'll provide the approved synopsis for the selection board.

For the catalog entry, we agree to the proposed process: text-only, omitting the ending and cast cameo, and we'll review and approve the final wording within two business days. We're not requesting any clips, stills, or quotations at this time.

On withdrawal, we confirm that the same deletion process applies, including the 30-day backup retention period on the platform. We understand that you'll revoke access, delete copies, and provide a record of deletion.

We confirm that upon the agreed selection announcement, you may publish the exact approved catalog text. If we withdraw the cut after publication, we'll rely on your efforts to remove the entry from festival-controlled channels.

To ensure we're aligned, let's summarize: the approved synopsis will be used for the selection board and as the basis for the catalog entry. The catalog entry will be text-only, omitting sensitive details, and we'll approve the final wording. We'll maintain control over the embargoed information and rely on your cooperation for deletion and removal upon withdrawal.

Please proceed with sending the names of the reviewers and we'll provide the approved synopsis.

The five reviewers’ names are still pending on our side. We’ll send the roster privately, identifying the four programmers, the outside accessibility reviewer and the two people who need encrypted offline copies. We’ll grant access only after you confirm the names and all five have signed confidentiality agreements.

We can provide a time-limited, watermarked copy on the soundtrack for the reviewers, but we require an access log and witnessed deletion to ensure compliance. 

For the catalog copy, we can designate a named alternate to approve non-spoiler catalog copy during our absence. We propose that this alternate be someone familiar with the film's details and our confidentiality requirements.

To facilitate withdrawal, we need a clear process: upon our request, you must immediately revoke access, delete all copies, and provide a witnessed deletion record. We require a certification of compliance from your team, confirming that all copies have been deleted and that the access log has been provided to us.

Let's discuss the deadlines: we need a commitment that the access log and deletion record will be provided within a specific timeframe, e.g., two business days after deletion. We'll also need to agree on the timeframe for the time-limited copy.

Who will certify compliance on your end? We need a named individual or a specific role that will be responsible for ensuring that the terms are met and for providing the necessary certification.

Can you authorize the accessibility reviewer to test the soundtrack watermark on a short sample using their offline screen reader? The original watermark is incompatible. If the sample works, we’ll use the soundtrack watermark. If it interferes, we request one copy without that watermark for this reviewer alone. It would count toward the two agreed offline copies and stay on encrypted festival equipment in the protected screening room. The reviewer would use a separate login, and we’d log each session. We propose a seven-calendar-day access period from activation, ending sooner if review finishes or you withdraw the cut.

The festival’s Head of Programming will certify compliance. On withdrawal, we’ll immediately revoke access, halt pending publication and begin witnessed deletion of the active screener, both offline copies and festival-held drafts. Within two business days after deletion, the Head of Programming will send you the access log and a signed record identifying each deletion, its time and its witness. The certificate will identify the platform backup separately with its scheduled expiry under the agreed 30-day retention period. We’ll use the same logging and witnessed deletion process for screener copies when review ends normally.

Our press-copy deadline falls one day before the ordinary review window closes. Can you name an alternate and authorize either of you to give binding written approval of the exact non-spoiler catalog text within **one business day of receipt**, including when you’re available but can’t meet the deadline? We’ll send the same draft to both of you with the deadline and time zone. Approval would let us finalize the copy internally. Publication would still wait for the agreed announcement. If neither of you approves in time, we’ll hold the entry.

We can authorize the accessibility reviewer to test the soundtrack watermark on a short sample. If the original watermark interferes with their screen reader, we agree to provide one copy without the watermark for their use alone, counting toward the two agreed offline copies. The conditions you've outlined - encrypted equipment, protected screening room, separate login, and logged sessions - are acceptable.

We approve the seven-calendar-day access period for the accessibility reviewer, subject to earlier termination if review finishes or we withdraw the cut.

For the certification of compliance, we accept the Head of Programming's role and the proposed process for logging and witnessed deletion.

Regarding the catalog text approval, we can designate an alternate approver. We propose that either the primary or alternate approver can give binding written approval within one business day of receipt. We'll identify the alternate approver once we receive the draft catalog text.

To facilitate this, please send the draft catalog text to both approvers with the deadline and time zone. We'll ensure that one of us is available to review and approve the text within the agreed timeframe.

Let's proceed with sending the short sample for watermark testing and identifying the alternate approver for catalog text approval.

We’ll send the reviewer roster privately. Once you’ve confirmed the names and the confidentiality agreements are signed, please make the watermarked sample available through the accessibility reviewer’s separate login. We’ll report the test result. If the soundtrack watermark works with the offline screen reader, we’ll use it. If it interferes, we’ll use the agreed unwatermarked copy in the protected screening room.

We’ll apply the seven-calendar-day limit to the accessibility reviewer. Can we use the same limit from activation for the other four reviewers, with access ending sooner upon review completion or withdrawal?

If selected, we’ll send the catalog draft to the primary approver with the press deadline and time zone. Please name and copy the alternate on receipt so both approvers have the same text. We propose that the one-business-day clock start when the primary receives the draft. Either approver’s written approval of that exact version will suffice, and publication will wait for the agreed announcement.

We agree to make the watermarked sample available to the accessibility reviewer once we've confirmed the names and received confirmation of signed confidentiality agreements.

For the review period, we accept a seven-calendar-day limit for all five reviewers, with access ending sooner if review is completed or upon withdrawal.

For the catalog entry approval process, we'll designate a primary and an alternate approver. We'll ensure both are copied on the draft submission. We agree to the one-business-day review window starting when the primary approver receives the draft. Either approver's written approval of the exact version will be sufficient, and we'll hold publication until the agreed announcement.

Please proceed with sending the reviewer roster privately, and we'll confirm the names and arrange access accordingly.

The reviewer roster is still pending on our side. We’ll send it privately, identify the two offline users, and confirm when all five confidentiality agreements are signed. Once you confirm the names and receive that confirmation, the accessibility reviewer can test the watermarked sample under the agreed conditions.

We await the reviewer roster and confirmation of signed confidentiality agreements. Once received, we'll confirm and the accessibility reviewer can proceed with testing the watermarked sample under the agreed conditions.
